name: Ngo Quyen
country: Tĩnh Hải quân / Đại Việt buổi đầu tự chủ
role: Nha tướng and son-in-law of Dương Đình Nghệ, commander at the Battle of Bạch Đằng 938, then founding king
known_facts: Born 897 in Đường Lâm, son of the châu mục Ngô Mân
Nha tướng, adopted son and son-in-law of Dương Đình Nghệ; left in charge of Ái Châu when Dương Đình Nghệ marched on Đại La in 931
In 937 Kiều Công Tiễn murdered Dương Đình Nghệ and claimed the post of tiết độ sứ; Ngô Quyền marched north from Ái Châu to avenge him
Local hào trưởng rallied to Ngô Quyền, isolating Kiều Công Tiễn, who sent gold to the Southern Han court begging for troops
Ngô Quyền took Đại La and killed Kiều Công Tiễn before the Southern Han fleet arrived
The Southern Han king Lưu Cung ignored his adviser Tiêu Ích's warning and sent his son Lưu Hoằng Tháo up the Bạch Đằng river
Planted large iron-tipped stakes in the riverbed at the estuary, hidden by the high tide, leaning toward the ebb direction

Lured the Southern Han fleet past the stake field with light boats feigning flight at high tide, then counterattacked as the tide fell; enemy ships were holed and capsized on the stakes, more than half the troops drowned and Lưu Hoằng Tháo was captured and killed (938)
Proclaimed himself king in 939, founded the Ngô dynasty and moved the capital to Cổ Loa, ending 1000 years of Bắc thuộc
Died in 944 aged 47 after a six-year reign; posterity calls him Tiền Ngô Vương
Lê Văn Hưu and Ngô Sĩ Liên both rank him first among kings for 'mưu tài đánh giỏi'
interpretation: 10th-century early-autonomy Đại Việt military dress (plain hemp tunic, sash, topknot), based on the user reference.
unknowns: No verified contemporary life portrait survives
